facts: p12-4a:An induction cooker has a coil under its glass top, carrying a rapidly changing
text:
An induction cooker has a coil under its glass top, carrying a rapidly changing current. A steel pan on top heats up, while the glass stays much cooler.
(i) What is produced in the base of the pan? [1]
(ii) Why does the pan get hot? [1]
(iii) Why doesn’t the glass top heat directly? [1]

points.text: (i) Eddy currents, induced by the changing magnetic flux.
(ii) The eddy currents dissipate energy as heat in the pan’s resistance.
(iii) Glass is an insulator, so almost no current is induced in it.

text: Using a phasor diagram, derive the expression for the impedance of a series LCR circuit.

points.text: Draw V_R in phase with I, V_L leading I by 90°, and V_C lagging I by 90°.
V_L and V_C are opposite, so their difference is V_L − V_C.
So V² = V_R² + (V_L − V_C)², by Pythagoras.
Dividing by I gives Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²).
Then tan φ = (X_L − X_C)/R gives the phase.

text: Show that the average power in an a.c. circuit is V_rms I_rms cos φ, and explain why it is zero for a pure inductor.

points.text: Instantaneous power is VI = V₀I₀ sin ωt sin(ωt − φ).
Averaging over a cycle leaves ½V₀I₀ cos φ.
That equals V_rms I_rms cos φ.
For a pure inductor, φ = 90°, so cos φ = 0.
So no average power is used.

why: The resonant frequency varies in inverse proportion to the capacitances square root, and the resonant frequency varies in inverse proportion to the inductances square root, so the factor is $0.5^{-0.5} \times 3^{-0.5}$ = 0.816.
